library.name: Concrete
library.text: First, concrete against your cheek. Then the taste of blood. Somewhere in the dark, water strikes metal. You reach for the last thing you remember before the fall. Nothing comes.

library.name: A Name
library.text: Lazarus. The name comes easily. Everything else asks for answers you do not have. Your jacket pockets are empty. A ragged hole gapes in the ceiling. Beyond it, a shaft of blackness.

library.name: No Sky
library.text: You pick up a stone and throw it overhead. One impact. Another. It falls back with a scatter of rubble. No ladder. No rope. You fell through a service duct, and its upper section has collapsed. Even if you remembered the way, you could not go back.

library.name: Red Light
library.text: A red lamp above the door blinks every few seconds. It shows you two things: the marks of your fall, and a dressing on your forearm. The bandage is clean. You cannot remember who put it there.

library.name: Examine the fall site
library.text: Search the rubble for something that might tell you where you came from.

library.name: Check the dressing
library.text: Start with your own body. It has been here the whole time.

library.name: Eight
library.text: A plate on a broken section of duct reads: ‘NEST / MEDICAL SECTOR / 08’. Level eight. If the numbers begin at the surface, there are at least seven floors of concrete above you.

library.name: A Trace
library.text: A single furrow cuts through the dust. It ends beneath your back. You try to retrace the fall and find only an absence, like reaching for a stair that is not there. You take a short metal rod from the rubble.

library.name: The Knot
library.text: The dressing is tied behind your arm, too neatly for you to have managed with your other hand. Beneath it lies a shallow cut. Fresh. Someone tended to you after the fall.

library.name: Stay Awake
library.text: Inside your cuff, someone has written: ‘DON’T SLEEP AGAINST THE WALL’. The letters are uneven, but familiar. Yours? You focus on your breathing. The pain becomes something you can contain.

library.name: Metal Rod
library.text: A short rod torn from the ductwork. One end is flattened. It could pry open a cover or a bolt.

library.name: The Last Shift
library.text: The door gives beneath your shoulder. Beyond it: a first-aid station, two chairs, a cup stained dry, an open cabinet. Disinfectant hangs in the air. Take whatever you think will help.

library.name: Electrolyte Ampoule
library.text: A clear, single-use ampoule with its seal intact. You break it open and drink the water and electrolytes, recovering up to 2 energy as you collect it.

library.name: Rubber Wedge
library.text: A heavy rubber doorstop. It could hold a spring-loaded door open—or keep one shut.

library.name: Ada’s ID Badge
library.text: ADA SHULZ / INFIRMARY. The strap is torn. On the back, someone has pencilled: ‘Oskar — engine room’. The badge may open the medical access door.

library.name: Nest
library.text: On the wall: ‘THE NEST — INFIRMARY’. Chairs stand beneath a duty roster. At the far end of the corridor is a service door. Something knocks steadily on the other side. You can look around here or approach the door.

library.name: Read the duty terminal
library.text: A green cursor still blinks. Find out what happened in the infirmary.

library.name: Look in the changing room
library.text: The sleeve of a medical coat hangs from a half-closed locker.

library.name: Try the stairs up
library.text: A blue arrow points towards the stairwell. You have to try.

library.name: Approach the service door
library.text: Leave the waiting room and find a way through.

library.name: Kogler
library.text: PATIENT RECORD: VICTOR KOGLER. 14 JAN 2041. ‘Headache. Increasing aggression. Rapid tissue growth. Patient screaming about butterflies. Consultation requested: Dr Steinfeld.’

library.name: Alarm
library.text: Below it, a security notice: ‘All available personnel to level 8. Come armed. This is not a drill.’ The terminal clock stopped at 03:17. You do not know whether the date means yesterday, or a world that no longer exists.

library.name: Advice
library.text: Someone has added a note in the margin: ‘They respond to sound. Do not attempt verbal reassurance.’ You commit it to memory.

library.name: Ada
library.text: A dead woman sits inside the locker. Ada is embroidered on her coat. An empty loop marks where her badge should be. The body looks only hours old. Dust lies a finger thick on the handle.

library.name: The Last Recording
library.text: Your fingers find a button on a small recorder in her coat pocket. ‘I shut down the lifts. The stairs are barricaded. Oskar went to the engine room to check the main gate power. He was supposed to be back ten hours ago.’

library.name: After the Voice
library.text: ‘There’s no way out. I can hear them getting closer.’ Cloth rustles. The recording ends. You close the locker gently, holding the metal door until it settles into place.

library.name: Sealed
library.text: The stairwell ends after two flights. An overturned ceiling slab blocks the way above. The lift doors stand ajar, but the car is gone; severed cables hang in the shaft. You will not see the surface from here.

library.name: Protocol
library.text: The panel reads: ‘LOCKDOWN. External access blocked. Local control disabled.’ Beneath it, a diagram shows a power line running from the engine room down into the complex. You return to the waiting room. At least you stop listening for wind.

library.name: Tremor
library.text: Nausea takes you at the service door. The concrete trembles beneath your fingers, though the pipes are silent. For a second, you are certain someone behind the wall is breathing in perfect time with you.

library.name: Count your breaths
library.text: Try to separate what you feel from what you can actually hear.

library.name: Step back and wait
library.text: Sit in the middle of the corridor. It will cost you some energy, but you can face this from a distance.

library.name: Breath
library.text: In. Out. Slowly, the rhythms drift apart. One was yours. The other comes from a ventilation duct. The nausea recedes. Now you know what to listen for.

library.name: Lazarus
library.text: You hear your name. You turn too quickly and catch your wound on the doorframe. The corridor is empty. You bite your lip and wait for your vision to settle. That voice was no memory.

library.name: Distance
library.text: You sit until the metallic taste fades. Away from the wall, it is easier. As you straighten your sleeve, you notice the writing inside the cuff: ‘DON’T SLEEP AGAINST THE WALL’. Someone has already tested that. You rise slowly.

library.name: The Courier
library.text: Through the door’s window, a uniformed man circles a trolley piled with parcels. One sleeve hangs empty. A growth on his neck moves a moment behind the rest of him. Every fourth step, his hip strikes the trolley. So that is the knocking.

library.name: Move with the knocks
library.text: The note warned you against speaking. Take each step only when the trolley strikes the wall.

library.name: Wait for the pause in his breathing
library.text: You recognise the rhythm from the vent. Slip past the courier when he stops to draw breath.

library.name: Slip behind the trolley
library.text: Risk passing close before he turns again.

library.name: Squeeze into the drain
library.text: The grate is loose. The drain goes around the door, but crawling will strain your wounded arm.

library.name: Delivery
library.text: You pass the trolley. A parcel reads: ‘Medical sector — deliver by hand’. The courier stops beside the wall. For a moment, he looks like a man who has forgotten why he entered a room. You do not wait for him to remember.

library.name: Movement
library.text: Your boot catches a wrapper. The courier turns his head. Before you can straighten up, he is on you. You shove the trolley between you and stumble into a side passage.

library.name: The Spring
library.text: The door slams behind you. Something strikes the other side. Once. Again. You hold the handle until silence falls. Your arm is bleeding. You are alive.

library.name: The Drain
library.text: The drain smells of rust. You cradle your wounded arm against your chest. Above you, the trolley knocks again and again. At the final grate, the sound fades. You drag yourself onto the floor beyond the service door, a few metres short of the medical airlock.

library.name: The Bolt
library.text: The airlock to the back rooms is shut. Its badge reader glows amber. Beside it, the drive mechanism’s cover hangs open. A low hatch for soiled linen sits beneath the wall: cramped, but clear.

library.name: Scan Ada’s badge
library.text: The reader still has power. See if it remembers its owner.

library.name: Pry the bolt with the rod
library.text: Slide the flattened end into the drive mechanism. The metal should hold.

library.name: Bridge the emergency circuit
library.text: Trace the wires and try to power the bolt. Costs 1 energy.

library.name: Crawl through the linen hatch
library.text: Leave the airlock alone. The narrow passage will cost you some energy.

library.name: Welcome
library.text: ‘WELCOME, ADA SHULZ’. The reader recognises the badge at once. The door opens with a soft hiss. For a moment, you wait for the system to notice its mistake. It never does.

library.name: Weight
library.text: The rod bends under the bolt’s weight. A few millimetres are enough. You squeeze through before the metal springs back. On the other side, a long tone sounds like a call no one will answer.

library.name: What Hands Remember
library.text: You choose the right wires before you can explain why. The bolt snaps back. You cannot remember who you were. Your hands, apparently, remember something.

library.name: A Spark
library.text: A spark burns your fingers. The mechanism falls silent. You wait for the smell of insulation to fade, then force yourself through the linen hatch. On the far side, you rest on cold tiles.

library.name: On Your Knees
library.text: You crawl for a long time. In the dark, your hand finds a discarded clog. You push it aside and shoulder the grate open. You spill into the back rooms. Up close, the calling tone sounds almost like a voice.

library.name: Contact
library.text: An old communications terminal stands in the back room. A green line trembles across its screen. You press a key. The tone breaks off halfway through a note. ‘Can anyone hear me? This is Juno-1. Emma Krause.’

library.name: Someone
library.text:
‘Hello?’ you answer.

A long breath at the other end.

‘Ada?’
‘No. Lazarus.’
‘Are you in Nest?’

You look at the sign above the door.

‘I think so. I don’t know how I got here.’

library.name: Two Days
library.text:
‘I hid aboard the ship when it started. Then the cryogenic sequence began. I’ve been trying to reach someone for two days.’

‘What level are you calling from?’

‘Level? Lazarus, I’m on Juno. In orbit.’

Behind you, something presses the door handle.

library.name: The Question
library.text: ‘I have to switch to the emergency channel,’ Emma says. ‘If you’re in the infirmary, Ada Shulz is there. Do you know her? Please. Tell me someone else is still alive.’

library.name: Tell her what you found
library.text: ‘I found Ada in the changing room. I’m sorry.’ Do not offer Emma hope you do not have.

library.name: Say you don’t know
library.text: ‘I haven’t found anyone I can talk to.’ Stay with what you know.

library.name: Promise to look for her
library.text: ‘I’ll check the infirmary when it’s safe to go back.’ For now, you need to get away from that door.

library.name: A Name
library.text:
Emma is silent for a long time.

‘She called me Em. No one else did.’

Then her practical voice returns.

‘Thank you for telling me. Listen carefully now. Stay away from the main lifts.’

library.name: An Honest Answer
library.text:
‘I understand,’ Emma says, though you hear that she had hoped for another word. ‘If you see her, tell her I waited.’

The handle behind you lowers again.

‘Lazarus? What was that? Stay away from the main lifts.’

library.name: Later
library.text:
‘All right. Just don’t take the risk now.’

Emma believes you so easily that, for a moment, you cannot answer.

‘Find somewhere safe first,’ she adds. ‘Stay away from the main lifts.’

library.name: The Engine Room
library.text:
‘Lockdown sealed the external access points. You can’t open them from there,’ Emma says. ‘Oskar was trying to restore power to the gates. Look for yellow service cables. They lead to the engine room.’

‘So, down?’

‘For now, down.’

library.name: Emergency Channel
library.text:
‘If you reach the switch room, bring up channel seven. I’ll be listen—’

Her voice stretches thin and vanishes. The screen reads: ‘JUNO-1 / TIME SYNC LOST’. Beside the door, you notice a hatch with a yellow cable. In the opposite wall is a linen storeroom.

library.name: The Handle
library.text: The handle lowers a third time. You can descend through the service hatch or hide in the storeroom. The way up is sealed. This choice is only about how you survive the next few hours.

library.name: Follow the yellow cable down
library.text: Leave the terminal. Emma has given you a direction, and a reason to move.

library.name: Wedge the door and descend
library.text: Drive the wedge beneath the door to buy time. You will leave it here.

library.name: Hide in the storeroom
library.text: Push a shelving unit across the entrance. Rest before trying to reach the engine room.

library.name: Level Eight
library.text: You lower yourself into the hatch. As your head drops below the floor, the back-room door crashes open. You do not look up. The yellow cable vanishes between the rungs below.

library.name: Someone Is Waiting
library.text:
Your memory has not returned. You have found no way out. But somewhere above the earth, a woman named Emma is waiting for your voice. You repeat it to yourself: channel seven.

End of chapter: AWAKENING.
Next objective: reach the engine room.

library.name: The Wedge
library.text: You drive the wedge in with your heel. When something pushes against the door, the rubber squeals, but holds. You descend more steadily, testing each rung. For the first time since waking, you decide when to move.

library.name: Seven
library.text:
At the bottom, you hear two blows. Then silence. You have a few minutes’ head start. You follow the yellow cable. Emma will be listening on channel seven.

End of chapter: AWAKENING.
Next objective: reach the engine room.

library.name: Shelter
library.text: Inside the storeroom, you slide a shelving unit across the door. You sit on folded sheets, away from the wall. Footsteps come down the corridor. They stop at the terminal. You wait for them to leave.

library.name: A Plan
library.text:
You do not know whether morning exists underground. You make a plan anyway: rest, yellow cable, engine room, channel seven. You repeat it so you will not lose one more thing.

End of chapter: AWAKENING.
Next objective: reach the engine room.

library.name: Sterile dressing
library.text: A sealed dressing and a single-use disinfectant swab. Clean the cut beneath your bandage before moving on.

nodes.name: 08B · A Voice That Is Not Yours
